title: auto-hypothesis-prober-for-version-pins
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight, priority-aware automated prober that fires hypothesis-driven evals when a model version is pinned or upgraded in either the catalog or tenant lock. This prober should run targeted, cost-bounded checks that detect regressions in functional correctness, instruction-following fidelity, hallucination rate, and latency distributions before the pin completes rollout.

Why: existing manual preflight and ad-hoc smoke suites are slow and miss tenant-specific failure modes. We need an automated mechanism that: (1) picks a small but representative set of probes per tenant or catalog change, (2) applies delta thresholds (not just absolute checks) to detect regressions vs the pinned baseline, and (3) classifies severity so that downstream automation can canary, block, or rollback pins.

Scope: the prober covers both catalog promotions and tenant-initiated pins. It is not responsible for full-scale synthetic eval jobs; instead it orchestrates fast probes (synthetic prompts + sampled shadow traffic) and returns structured signals to the eval-orchestrator service. The implementation will include priority lanes: CATALOG_HIGH, TENANT_CRITICAL, TENANT_LOW, with different sampling budgets and thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Prober runs automatically on any model version pin event (catalog or tenant) and returns a structured verdict within configured time window
Supports priority lanes with configurable budget and delta thresholds
Delta-based checks compare new model to pinned baseline for a tenant or catalog canonical baseline
Outputs include: signal summary (pass/warn/fail), sample examples for inspection, metric diffs (accuracy proxies, hallucination rate, latency P95), and cost used
Integration tests for both synthetic probes and shadow traffic sampling are added to CI
Product and Security sign-off on rollout policy and KMS usage for any tenant test data
implementation_notes: Use existing eval-harness runner but add a lightweight 'prober' profile that limits corpus size and model tokens

Priority lanes map: CATALOG_HIGH => conservative thresholds, higher sample budget; TENANT_CRITICAL => tenant-owned baseline comparison and tighter thresholds; TENANT_LOW => fast smoke with lenient thresholds
Delta thresholds expressed as percent delta or absolute delta depending on metric (e.g., hallucination rate > +3pp triggers warn, +7pp triggers fail)
Budget-aware sampling: default cost cap per probe and tenant-exempt list for high-value customers
Fallback path: when prober fails to complete within timeout, flag as WARN and attach why (timeout/infra-error)
Ship metadata to console: per-pin verdict, sample artifacts (redacted), and link to full eval job when scheduled
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives due to small sample sizes — Mitigation: use delta thresholds and require corroboration across multiple probes
Risk: cost runaway if tenant pins trigger large probes — Mitigation: enforce per-probe cost caps and tenant budget policies
Risk: leaking tenant data into catalog-level probes — Mitigation: always redact PII and ensure tenant probes run in tenant-scoped environment with KMS
Risk: blocking promotions due to transient infra flakiness — Mitigation: add transient-failure retries and distinguish infra failures from model regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for prober orchestration and verdict logic
Integration test: simulate a catalog pin event and assert CATALOG_HIGH lane runs and produces verdict within 5 minutes
Sandbox tenant test: tenant pin with synthetic prompts plus shadowed 1% production traffic for 60s, assert signal stability
Load test: run 100 concurrent prober jobs to validate scheduler backpressure and cost accounting
Post-rollout validation: sample 10 customer pins in canary region and compare prober verdicts to full eval run results
notes: Discussion with infra (Mar 2): prefer reuse of eval-orch queue and add a prober priority class
Design feedback (Mar 4, Aisha Patel): add tenant exemption/opt-out via tenant settings and surfaced in Console
Security review checklist drafted in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/Prober+Security
Dashboard prototype for prober verdicts: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/prober/verdicts (mock)
